svg.title: Visualization of the Fourier Transform
svg.desc: An infographic explaining how a signal in time can be represented as a sum of sine waves and converted into a frequency spectrum using the Fourier transform.
svg.text: Fourier Transform: turning a signal into its frequencies

text.tspan: The Fourier transform asks: “Which sine waves are hidden inside this signal, and how strong are they?”
It converts a waveform from the time domain into a frequency-domain spectrum.
A measured signal changes over time.
Here it contains slow and fast oscillations mixed together.
Complicated in time, but often simple in frequency.
The transform reveals the hidden ingredients.
Strong matches mean those frequencies are present.

svg.text: If a basis wave lines up with the signal, its coefficient is large.

text.tspan: So the waveform is re-expressed as:
Instead of showing change over time,
the spectrum shows energy at each frequency.
That is why Fourier methods help with filtering,

svg.text: Time domain = “what happens when?” • Frequency domain = “what frequencies are present?”
